svg.title: Figure 2. Horizontal shear and the shearing-stress distribution
svg.desc: Three panels. (a) A short length delta x of a beam, cut horizontally above the neutral axis. The normal stresses on the part above the cut are larger on the right face, where the moment is M plus delta M, than on the left, so a horizontal force delta H equal to q times delta x must act on the cut; the shaded area above the cut is A prime with its centroid at y bar prime. (b) In a rectangle the shearing stress varies as a parabola through the depth, zero at the top and bottom and largest, 3V over 2A, at the neutral axis. (c) In an I-section the stress is small in the flanges, jumps up where the width drops to the web thickness, and is nearly uniform across the web.
